coverage: Worldwide config/global_bounds.json (lon -180..180, lat -90..90, 3600x1800) + NA nest. No shoreline cut. Gaps transparent.
display_units: dBZ-equivalent qualitative intensity (IEM domain) + compatible ECCC intensity (outside IEM domain)
eccc_units: rain mm/h, snow cm/h (precipitation RATE, not dBZ — not numerically interchangeable with IEM)
freshness_label: LIVE / CURRENT OBSERVATION (NEXRAD + ECCC NA radar, 5-6 min mosaic)

iem_effective_domain.note: Effective CONUS NEXRAD network coverage inside the advertised GetCapabilities bbox (lon -171..170, lat 5..70). Authoritative footprint source: IEM WMS GetCapabilities LatLonBoundingBox; effective radar coverage further limited to the WSR-88D network.

precedence: ECCC rain (rates -> dBZ via NWS Z=300R^1.4 onto the original N0Q key) wins everywhere its RADAR_COVERAGE_*.INV dynamic coverage is valid, including most of CONUS; ECCC snow renders in the blue snow ramp at the same severity rank ONLY where Radar_1km_SfcPrecipType classifies snow (mixed/freezing rain render on the dBZ key); IEM N0Q (native rendering, itself the original legend, type undifferentiated) fills ECCC gaps; 10-px cross-fade on the coverage edge; radar-only composite (no cloud underlay, no model fill); transparent elsewhere.
source_name: Iowa Environmental Mesonet CONUS NEXRAD N0Q base reflectivity (NOAA WSR-88D) inside its domain + ECCC North American Radar Composite 1km rain (RADAR_1KM_RRAI, mm/h) / snow (RADAR_1KM_RSNO, cm/h) / precipitation type (Radar_1km_SfcPrecipType) outside it
title: LIVE PRECIPITATION
variable: N0Q base reflectivity dBZ (IEM domain gaps); ECCC precipitation-rate rain (mm/h)/snow (cm/h) mapped to dBZ through the ECCC 14-color class rates with the NWS Z=300R^1.4 equivalence (equal ECCC colors = equal severity = equal dBZ for rain and snow); ECCC SfcPrecipType gates snow-blue rendering. One 5-75 dBZ key for rain + 8-step blue snow ramp at matched severity.
visual_note: IEM palette preserved in its domain. ECCC rain mapped to the same 11-step key qualitatively; ECCC snow mapped to the 8-step blue snow ramp at matched severity. GDPS model fill renders translucent (pale) so it never reads as observed radar. Equal colors across the transition do NOT claim identical measurements.
